rows.title_full: AN ACT EXTENDING COLLEGE SCHOLARSHIP ASSISTANCE TO THE DEPENDENTS OF THE ACTIVE MEMBERS OF THE POLICE, MILITARY, FIRE AND JAIL BUREAU
rows.abstract: It is herein provided a college scholarship assistance to the dependents of the active uniformed personnel of the police, military, fire and jail bureau, under the following conditions: (a) That college scholarship assistance shall be limited only to a maximum of three (3) dependents per active member; (b) That dependents shall be given full scholarship in any state tertiary educational instituion: Provided, that they meet the qualifications set forth by the institution; (c) That at least five(5) slots in the CHED Scholarship Program for each congressional district shall be alloted for these dependents; Provided, that in cases where there are more than five (5) dependents; and (d) That in circumstances where dependents are unable to availl of the privileges stipulated in the last two preceding paragraphs in this same section, they shall be entitled to a scholarship grant in a private but non-exclusive college or tertiary educational institution, subject to the evaluation and requirem

rows.abstract: This bill seeks to include parapsychology in the curriculum to enable the youth to widen their educational horizon and perspectives. It will help them understand occurrences or phenomena outside the natural order of things. Likewise, parapsychologyas a subject in the curruculum will enable individuals with this natural ability to develop their psychic and extraordinary powers for their over-all advancement.

rows.abstract: Rationale: In view of the delay in the approval of the FY 2001 General Appropriations Bill, it is necessary to enact legislation to meet urgent budgetary requirements which cannot be postponed without causing detriment to government operations. Onesuch requirement is the passage of a supplemental budget for the national government which will be needed foremost to provide authority for expenditures that are not in the reenacted budget but are either mandatory by virtue of law or necessary for the welfare of our public servants. It will also augment priority expenditures that cannot be sufficiently covered by the reenacted budget.
rows.status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09137) enacted on 2001-06-08

This bill therefore seeks to establish a Ports and Harbors Office under the Department of Transportation and Communication which will provide a continuing and lasting commitment to the overall developmentof feeder ports and the relevant facilities nationwide.

rows.author: C059
rows.title_full: AN ACT COMPLYING WITH THE CONSTITUTIONAL MANDATE TO RENDER A MEASURE OF JUSTICE TO THE VICTIMS OF HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS AS A CONSEQUENCE OF THE PROCLAMATION OF MARTIAL LAW, AND THEREAFTER, BY COMPENSATING THEM, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: All bona fide victims of human rights violations, such as salvaging, disappearances, torture, rape, unlawful arrest, indefinite detention without charges, and the like are entitled to compensation as a matter of constitutional rights and of plain and simple justice and may file claims for the purpose.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL, POLITICAL AND HUMAN RIGHTS since 2001-06-06

rows.author: C059
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PROTECTION AND CONSERVATION OF ALL OBJECTS OF UNDERWATER CULTURAL HERITAGE IN PHILIPPINE WATERS
rows.abstract: "Protection of Underwater Cultural Heritage Act." This bill aims to protect and preserve our underwater cultural heritage by providing for general requirements for underwater archaeology, exploration, and excavation, the description of the items tobe protected, prohibition of certain activities in the vicinity of a protected item and site, the establishment of a reward system for verified reports, and the imposition of sanction penalties for violations.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION since 2001-06-06

rows.author: C059
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING A CHILDREN'S WELFARE FUND FOR THE PROTECTION AND REHABILITATION OF ABANDONED, ABUSED AND SEXUALLY EXPLOITED CHILDREN, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED 7610, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS `THE SPECIAL PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AGAINST CHILD ABUSE, EXPLOITATION AND DISCRIMINATION ACT'
rows.abstract: Our Constitution explicitly declares that it is the duty of the State to defend the rights of the children, assist and protect them from all forms of neglect, abuse, cruelty, exploitation and other conditions prejudicial to their development. Pursuant to this constitutional mandate, this measure seeks to establish a fund to be managed by the Department of Social Welfare and Development which shall be used mainly for the protection and rehabilitation of abandoned, abused and sexually exploited children.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SOCIAL SERVICES since 2001-06-06

rows.author: C059
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO RATIONALIZE THE ADMINISTRATION AND ENFORCEMENT OF ALL LAWS ON OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY AND HEALTH STANDARDS AND ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill proposed to identify the lead agency which will be responsible for coordinating and overseeing the activities of all agencies that are involved in the promotion of occupational safety and health standards and environmental protection programs.  It also seeks to authorize the lead agency, after consultations with participating agencies and sectors concerned, to prescribe administrative fines in cases of violations of such standards and regulations.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-06-06

rows.author: C059
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PHASE-OUT OF PLASTIC BAGS AS PACKING MATERIALS OF GOODS SOLD OR DISPOSED BY SARI-SARI STORES, MARKET VENDORS, DEPARTMENT STORES AND SIMILAR ESTABLISHMENTS, PRESCRIBING PENALTIES THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The use of plastic bags as packing materials of goods sold by sari-sari stores, market vendors, department stores and similar establishments is hereby prohibited after the phase out period as determined by this Act. The use of plastic bags shall bephased out within a period of three from the effectivity of this Act.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2001-06-06

rows.author: C059
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE USE OF RECYCLABLE MATERIALS FOR THE PACKAGING OF CONSUMER PRODUCTS TO BE SOLD COMMERCIALLY, PROVIDING MECHANISMS THEREFORE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Under this bill, the State shall require and encourage the use of biodegradable and recyclable materials in the packaging of consumer products in order to reduce solid waste genration.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2001-06-06

rows.author: C059
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR ACCOUNTABILITY AND TRANSPARENCY IN THE FOREIGN TRAVEL OF PUBLIC OFFICERS AND EMPLOYEES PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: It is hoped tht through this bill all official foreign travels should henceforthm be measured strictly in terms of the larger national interest -conservation of scarce foreign exchange and national resources for the basic needs of our struggling masses.  The government expenditure for official travels should thus be cut to the bone. limited to those involving real national interest and verboten for expenditures that are more for personall aggrandizement and gratification than the good of the public.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-06-06

rows.author: C059
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A NATIONAL ECOTOURISM POLICY, ESTABLISHING A FRAMEWORK FOR ITS INSTITUTIONALIZ ATION AND CREATING AN INSTITUTIONAL MECHANISM FOR ITS IMPLEMENTATION AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "National Ecotourism Policy Act of 1991."  This bill proposes an ecotourism policy that would lay down a tourism framework based on a well-crafted balance between economic growth and environmental protection. It creates a National Ecotourism Commission which shall formulate and implement an Ecotourism Masterplan with the assistance of the Department of Tourism and the Department of Environment and Natural Resources. There shall also be created in the bill a network of ecotourism sites which would include but not limited to the Integrated Protected Areas System under R.A. No. 7586.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TOURISM since 2001-06-06

rows.author: C059
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE EXACTION OF FEES AND UNNECESSARY SERVICES FROM JOB APPLICANTS
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to prohibit employers/recru iters to require from job applicants as requisite to employment, the following: (a) The payment of any fees for whatever purpose or reason except where the exaction of such fee has been authorized by the Secretary of Labor and Employment and/or by law; (b) To render any service unrelated to the position being applied for; and (c) To submit unreasonable requirement. A requirement is unreasonable when it is illegal or immoral, or unrelated to or undeterminative of the acceptance of the application.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-06-06

rows.author: C059
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO DEFINE AND PENALIZE CONSPIRACIES AND COMBINATIONS IN PUBLIC BIDDINGS, PREVENT ILLEGAL SCHEMES AND FRAUDS, ENSURE FAIRNESS AND FREE COMPETITION AND SAFEGUARD THE INTEREST OF THE GOVERNMENT
rows.abstract: "The Competitive Public Bidding Act of 1995." Towards this end, the State shall ensure competitive, open and fair public biding in all government contracts, prevent collusion, fraud and favoritism, and realize the most economical, advantageous and favorable terms for the government.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOOD GOVERNMENT since 2001-06-06

rows.author: C059
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR BENEFITS AND PRIVILEGES TO SOLO PARENTS AND THEIR CHILDREN AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Solo Parents Welfare Act." This Act aims to promote the family as the foundation of the nation, strengthen its solidarity and ensure its total development. Towards this end, it shall develop a comprehensive program of services for solo parents andtheir children to be carried out by the Department of Social Selfare and Development (DSWD), the Department of Health (DOH) and other related government and non-government agencies.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SOCIAL SERVICES since 2001-06-06

rows.author: C059
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 209, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE FAMILY CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill proposes a radical innovation that seeks to lessen the undesirable impact of being born outside of wedlock. However, it limits its beneficiaries to natural children alone for the reasons discussed above.  It pursues and pushes the conceptof legitimation beyond its traditional acceptance. The rationale is to provide maximum protection to the innocent child and thus safeguard his welfare and future.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on POPULATION AND FAMILY RELATIONS since 2001-06-06

rows.author: C059
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING HIGHER COMPENSATION TO VICTIMS OF UNJUST IMPRISONMENT OR DETENTION AND VICTIMS OF VIOLENT CRIMES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 4 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7309, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Hence, this bill seeks to amend Section 4 of R.A. No. 7309 by increasing the amount be awarded to the victims of unjust imprisonment of detention as well as victims of violent crimes.  The proposed measure, therefore, provides that those who have been unjustly imprisoned or detained for less than five (5) years shall be entitled to receive P1,000.00 for every month of such imprisonment. However, for those who were imprisoned for more than five (5) years are entitled to claim P2,000.00 for everymonth of such imprisonment or detention. While the compensation for the victims of violent crimes is increased from P10,000.00 to P100,000.00 considering the high cost of hospitalization and medical treatment.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-06-06

rows.author: C059
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ENSURE THE SAFETY OF AUTOMATED MACHINE TELLER (ATM) USERS BY PRESCRIBING CERTAIN SECURITY MEASURES
rows.abstract: Regardless of location, safety measures shall be set up by the owner bank in the establishment of automated Teller Machine (ATM) in order to protect the safety of the user. All ATMs shall be situated in an enclosed area where the clients are given ample privacy to conduct their respective business. Security personnel shall also be provided within the vicinity,
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 2001-06-06

rows.author: C059
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE SERVICE OF WARRANTS OF ARRESTS IN CERTAIN CASES AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF
rows.abstract: Except only in cases of citizen's arrest, arrest of persons made as a result of surveillance and/or entrapment operations; persons being arrested for subversion and other crimes and offenses against national security; notorious and dangerous criminals for whom outstanding warrants of arrest have been issued; and escapist and fugitives from justice, it is hereby prohibited to service warrants of arrests during nighttime, on legal holidays, or on weekends.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-06-06

rows.author: C059
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING BEREAVEMENT LEAVE OF FIVE (5) WORKING DAYS WITH PAY TO ALL EMPLOYEES OF THE GOVERNMENT AND THE PRIVATE SECTOR
rows.abstract: This provides that a Bereavement Leave of Five Working Days with Pay be offered as a benefit to all memners of the Government Service Insurance System (GSIS) and Social Security System (SSS). In so doing the employee is asured of adequate time considertation to take care of the needs attendant to the death of his loved one while providing him an opportunity to commiserate with his other relatives.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-06-06

rows.author: C059
rows.title_full: AN ACT ALLOWING MARRIED OR LEGALLY SEPARATED WOMEN TO USE THEIR MAIDEN FIRST NAME AND SURNAME, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLES THREE HUNDRED SEVENTY AND THREE HUNDRED SEVENTY-TWO OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED THREE HUNDRED EIGHTY-SIX, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE CIVIL CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Rationale:  By allowing Filipino women to retain their surnames as part of their individuality, even after marriage or legal separation, this bill seeks to translate into reality the concept of "fundamental equality" of men and women before the lawas enshrined in our Constitution.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WOMEN since 2001-06-06

rows.author: C059
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING ALL COLLEGES AND UNIVERSITIES TO PROVIDE SCHOLARSHIP GRANTS TO AT LEAST FIVE PERCENT (5%) OF THEIR STUDENT POPULATION WHO ARE POOR BUT DESERVING STUDENTS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "The Scholarship Program for Poor but Deserving Students Act." Scholarship grants are hereby granted in the form of free tuition fee only to at least five percent (5%) of the student population of all colleges and universities who are poor but deserving students.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2001-06-06

rows.author: C059
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A GRANT OF REWARD TO INFORMERS OF VIOLATIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7080 AND/OR REPUBLIC ACT NO. 1379 AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: In the said bill, the informer, who gives vital information supported by competent evidence which account for or materially aid in the recovery of forfeiture of ill-gotten wealth as defined under the aforecited laws, shall be entitled to a reward oftwenty-five percentum (25%) if the total value of the property actually recovered.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-06-06

rows.author: C059
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING THE GRANTING OF REWARDS AND PROTECTION TO THOSE WHO WILL REPORT MALFEASANCE IN GOVERNMENT OFFICES AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Any government employee who will report any act of malfeasance committed by his superior or any of his co-employees shall be granted a reward or incentive in terms of cash, bonus or promotion in rank, if qualified and shall be provided protection against any retaliation from erring officials oremployees.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOOD GOVERNMENT since 2001-06-06

rows.author: C059
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE INCLUSION OF LAW ENFORCEMENT AND COMMUNITY SERVICE COURSES IN THE CURRICULA OF ALL COLLEGES AND UNIVERSITIES, CONVERTING THE EXISTING COMPULSORY MILITARY TRAINING REQUIREMENTS AS OPTIONAL SUBJECTS ONLY, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Citizens Police Training and Community Service Act of 1998" All colleges and universities in the country, had to spend one afternoon a week marching around the school campus. The millions of Filipinos who have gone through this waste of time have yet to receive some plausible evidence for the dubious theory that training in close-order drill turns people into citizens - soldiers with the skills needed to fight the country's enemies. This is not to argue that all military training is useless.It is to declare, rather, that the kind of military training that has been given since World War II has been more suited for producing people who can march smartly in parades than infantry men who shoot straigth. When both trainors and trainees are eextremely skeptical about the usefulness of the program, there's little guilt about subverting the program.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2001-06-06

rows.author: C059
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL VOLUNTEER SERVICE PROGRAMME, STRENGTHENING GOVERNMENTAL MECHANISMS FOR THE REGULATION OF VOLUNTEER SERVICES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill aims to encourage the promotion of volunteer service programmes for national development, social welfare and international understanding; and maximize the benefits that may be derived from volunteer service programs.  It will support efforts of government agencies and the private sector in seeking the attainment of national development goals. >Thisproposed measure will establish a National Volunteer Service Programme to provide the necessary manpower and technical expertise for development projects undertaken in the country.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-06-06

rows.author: C059
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE IMPROVEMENT AND STRENGTHENING OF THE NATIONAL HISTORICAL INSTITUTE 1
rows.abstract: The National Historical Institute (NHI) shall be responsible for promoting and preserving the Philippine cultural heritage by undertaking, among others, studies on Philippine historyand Filipino heroes; encouraging historical educational activities,including the widening of local historical committee network; and managing and safeguarding the improvement and restoration of national shrines, monuments, historical sites, buildings and landmarks.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION since 2001-06-06

rows.author: C059
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING MANDATORY SCHOOL INSPECTIONS TO PROTECT THE HEALTH AND SAFETY OF STUDENTS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Notwithstanding any laws to the contrary, schools of all levels and training institutions are hereby required to conduct a yearly inspection of facilities relevant to the health and safety of the students and their teaching and non-teaching pesonnel, such as, but not limited to the following: water supply system, comfort rooms, cafeterias and restaurants and fire exits.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION since 2001-06-06

rows.author: A087
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING FAILURE OF ELECTIONS DUE TO LARGE SCALE VOTE BUYING AND VOTE SELLING
rows.abstract: "Electoral Reform Act of 2001." It is therefore imperative that the election process be reinvented to make vote-buying/sel ling at least a very risky practice for the candidate. A candidate who is losing or who has lost because of vote-buying/sel ling must be given the right to call for a suspension of proclamation prior to the proclamation of the winning candidate upon submission of evidence. This will effectively discourage would-be candidate-offen ders, who would not be given the satisfaction of being proclaimed winners as what happens in the present system.  In essence, this Act will effectively discourage candidates from buying their mandate from the people. A candidate will not run the high risk of losing his millions if it would bevery easy to effct a failure of elections by another candidate before the former's proclamation.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2001-06-06
